subject: Segmentation ownership matrix and diagram request for SOC2/SIG
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novaline.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: secops@novaline.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Segmentation ownership and diagram for SOC 2 / SIG

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this — our SOC 2 team asked for a concise mapping that shows who owns each segmentation boundary (control plane, data plane, egress, inter-region) for Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments. Specifically they want: 

- A single-page ownership matrix (service/zone -> team/contact)
- A basic diagram that shows zone demarcations and allowed traffic flows (we're fine with PNG/Draw.io)
- Notes about fallback routing and whether cross-tenant egress is possible between Dedicated pools

Can you share a short snapshot + any artifacts we can attach to the SIG questionnaire by EOD your time? If you can include any contact names we can pull into our evidence binder that would be ideal.

Attachments: none

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Security Program Manager | Novaline
alice.chen@novaline.com
secops@novaline.com

--
Alice asked: this is scoped to Dedicated and Private only (no hosted shared-tenancy).

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@novaline.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Segmentation ownership and diagram for SOC 2 / SIG

Hi Alice — thanks for the clarity. We'll put together a compact ownership matrix and a Draw.io-exported PNG with the zone boundaries and allowed flows. Quick clarifications so we tailor to your evidence binder: 

1) Do you want the matrix to include phone/Slack contacts or just owner names and email addresses?
2) For "fallback routing" — should we document our automated fallback (model variant/regional) policies or focus purely on network-level fallbacks (e.g., cross-region transit, peering)?

Plan: Kimberly will draft the matrix and diagram. Marcus will add a one-paragraph statement on "why cross-tenant egress is blocked by default" and the exceptions flow. We can deliver a ZIP with: XLSX matrix, PNG diagram, and a short narrative.

If EOD is tight for you, we'll prioritize the XLSX + PNG and follow up with the narrative tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Segregation ownership matrix + diagram (draft)

Hi Alice / Tessa,

Attached is a first draft: segregation_ownership_matrix_v1.xlsx and zonal-demarcation_v2.drawio.png. Deliverables at a glance: 

- segregation_ownership_matrix_v1.xlsx (tabbed):
  - Tab 1: Ownership matrix (Zone / Service / Primary owner / Contact / Escalation)
  - Tab 2: Traffic policy summary (allowed ingress/egress, ACLs, default deny rules)
  - Tab 3: Exception log template (how to request temporary egress)

- zonal-demarcation_v2.drawio.png: single-page diagram showing 
  - Control plane demarcation (control plane in a customer-managed VPC for Private deployments, isolated RGs for Dedicated)
  - Data plane (GPU pools, tenant lanes, KV cache boundaries)
  - Egress gates (KMS/HSM boundary, egress filtering zones)

Quick notes: 
- Cross-tenant egress is blocked by default at the hypervisor/network fabric level for Dedicated pools; only approved cross-tenant data flows are proxied via a tenant-to-tenant bridge node and require a documented exception (see Tab 3).
- Fallback routing: we document both the network fallback (regional peering + multi-region public NAT) and the inference-fallback policy (model-variant fallback) in the narrative file we'll add after your review.

Attachments: segregation_ownership_matrix_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), zonal-demarcation_v2.drawio.png (image/png)

Please review and let us know if you'd like different granularity (e.g., per-service ACLs expanded into a separate tab).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Architect | Redwood Inference

This is great — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of small asks from our SOC team after a quick skim: 

- In the ownership matrix, can you add a column for "Evidence location" (Drive link or HS ticket) so we can point reviewers directly to artifacts?
- On the diagram, can you label the egress gates with the KMS boundary and note whether KMS keys are customer-managed for Private deployments?

If you can add those two bits and resend, we'll attach to the SIG + CAIQ responses. The XLSX + PNG are perfect otherwise.

If it's easier, we can accept a one-page supplement in plain text.
